Amazon protection may have galvanised conservationists, but the far greater motivations for many Lula voters were record low unemployment, robust wage growth, a 15% increase in “bolsa familia” poverty relief payments and a promise to raise the minimum wage. The importance of combining social justice with climate and nature action is widely recognised by Brazilian environmental groups. Without it, elections are lost and protests can erupt in the streets – as the world learned from France during the violent gilets jaunes (yellow vests) demonstrations of 2018.
7 Defend sovereignty, democracy and sustainability. Lula and his army called out the interlinked threats posed by the Bolsonaro family’s fealty to Donald Trump (now doubly confirmed by Flávio’s post-election flight to the US). They highlighted the interlinked threats posed by the obsequience to Trump, Bolsonaro’s desire to change the constitution and his promise to open up exploration of the Amazon and other biomes. This reflects a global phenomenon. Now that seven of the planetary boundaries essential for the flourishing of life have been breached, more and more people are affected by business activities that make the situation worse by destabilising the climate, damaging ecosystems and polluting the air, soil and rivers. This makes it harder for extractive companies to secure a social mandate so they become more inclined to either break the law or support extreme politics that override democracy.
The former environment minister Marina Silva pulled these threads together during the victory celebrations, saying Brazil had come together against these threats: “Long live the people who emerged from every corner of Brazil to sow hope for a future that is socially just, sovereign, democratic and sustainable.”
Brazil has given the world a remarkable example of hope through action. Now it needs others to follow.

title: Eight of England’s nine water companies still failing on environment, report finds
content_c:
Angela Eagle, the environment secretary, has summoned water industry bosses to Whitehall after a report found that the environmental performance of the big companies has worsened despite investment.
“People are sick of excuses,” Dame Angela said, after the Environment Agency joined the Drinking Water Inspectorate, Natural Resources Wales and Ofwat for a joint report that rated eight of the nine water companies in England as “poor” or “requiring improvement”.
There were 74 serious pollution incidents, the category that causes significant harm to the environment, the report said. That was just one fewer than the previous year, despite billions of pounds of investment, bans on bosses’ bonuses and a public outcry. The watchdog’s environmental performance assessment ratings of water companies added up to 16 “stars” out of a possible 36, a fall from 19 the previous year, and the lowest score since the process began.
Changes could be imposed on the industry, Eagle warned: “Water companies have let the public down time and time again, and today’s report is further proof that root-and-branch reform cannot wait.”
The UK is one of only two countries in the world where the provision of water is fully privatised. The other is Chile, where water privatisation was imposed in the 1980s by a military dictatorship.
Overall, there were 2,666 pollution incidents in England in 2025 – a 40% increase on 2016, the EA said. Thames Water had the most, followed by Anglian Water, United Utilities, Yorkshire Water and Southern Water.
The Department for the Environment, Food and Rural Affairs (Defra) said Eagle was preparing to take “further action”, with “tougher consequences” for executives at failing companies.
Defra said it would “set out a clear set of improvement actions”, such as “tackling leakage”, “reductions in pollution incidents” and “improving customer satisfaction”. Rules that took effect last year would block bonuses for executives at companies receiving a one-star rating.
Environmental campaigners called for stronger action. “This is a system that rewards shareholders and creditors while our rivers, wildlife and bill payers lose out,” said James Wallace, the chief executive of River Action.
Thames Water, the worst offender, ought to go into special administration immediately, he said. “Ministers must end the failed privatisation experiment, review alternative models including public ownership, and give regulators the power to make polluters pay not the public.”
The four agencies have pooled their data in a joint report for the first time – a step towards combining currently fragmented regulatory responsibilities under a single watchdog. But Richard Benwell, the chief executive of Wildlife and Countryside Link, said a new regulator “must be more than a merger of existing institutions”.
“It needs a clear legal duty to restore nature, strong environmental targets and the powers and resources to enforce the law across the water industry, industrial agriculture, and chemical companies,” he said.
Water UK, the industry trade body, said: “Today’s report shows the lowest level of leakage in history, as well as other areas of good performance. However, the fact remains that the environmental performance of some water companies is not good enough.
“While more than half of all pollution incidents last year were caused by blockages or vandalism, which are not in the direct control of the water companies, there is clearly more work to do.
“It will take time, but record investment will help secure water supplies, support growth and end sewage entering rivers and seas.”

title: Binance crypto platform suspends trades amid suspected hack
content_c:
Binance crypto platform suspends trades amid suspected hack
October 30, 2026
The world's largest cryptocurrency platform, Binance, confirmed on Thursday that it was investigating a potential security breach that resulted in an estimated $6.3 billion impact.
Analysts said the breach could amount to the largest-ever crypto heist
"It does look like a hack on Binance," said former company chief Changpeng Zhao, who remains a major shareholder.
Binance said it worked to freeze the affected assets and that it had located about $3 billion so far. It did not provide information about the remaining $3.3 billion.
"Binance will cover all hacking losses," co-founder Yi He said, without providing more details about the incident.
Some $3 billion (€2.7 billion) had been frozen in response to the suspected hack.
Binance 'reviewing' possible hack
"Rest assured that user funds are completely safe," a company spokesperson said.
"Our security teams are reviewing all relevant information with urgency, and we will provide updates through official Binance channels as soon as we have verified information," the company statement said.
"Binance’s initial investigation suggests that the security incident may involve a compromised DevOps engineer’s laptop, which allowed an attacker to gain access to a service container and submit unauthorized withdrawal transactions," the company wrote. "We have found no evidence of any wallet private key leak."
The company, which is the world's largest platform in terms of daily crypto trading volume, suspended trading on certain products while the freezing came from cryptocurrency companies using the platform.
Tether froze around $1.6 billion in its USDT currency, according to CEO Paolo Ardoino, and Circle froze some $800 million-worth of USDC, boss Jeremy Allaire said.
Who is Binance ex-CEO Zhao?
The news of the possible hack sent Bitcoin's value tumbling by 3.2% on Thursday evening, dropping below $79,000.
Zhao, who founded the Binance platform in 2017, said "as a shareholder, I expect all user funds will be fully covered."
He stepped down as CEO after pleading guilty in 2023. to failing to prevent money laundering on his platform. US President Donald Trump pardoned him in 2025.
Zhao and Binance have been key supporters of cryptocurrency ventures by US President Donald Trump and his family.

title: Wahl in Israel: Alle Stimmen ausgezählt - Patt bleibt bestehen
content_c:
Wahl in Israel Alle Stimmen ausgezählt - Patt bleibt bestehen
Die Auszählung der Stimmen in Israel bestätigt, dass eine äußerst schwierige Regierungsbildung bevorsteht. Unterdessen ist ein Streit über das Wahlergebnis entbrannt - die Likud-Partei spricht von "gestohlener Wahl".
Auch nach der vollständigen Auszählung aller Stimmen steht kein klarer Sieger der Parlamentswahl in Israel fest: Weder die Regierungskoalition von Benjamin Netanjahu noch das Oppositionslager von Gadi Eisenkot konnten eine absolute Mehrheit erreichen. Das teilte die Zentrale Wahlkommission Israels in der Nacht mit.
Laut dem vorläufigen amtlichen Endergebnis kommt die bisherige Koalition aus rechten, rechtsextremen und religiösen Parteien auf 53 Sitze im Parlament (2022: 64 Sitze). Für eine Mehrheit bräuchte es 61 Mandate.
Als zweitstärkste Kraft geht den Angaben zufolge die von Eisenkot neu gegründete Mitte-Partei Jaschar mit 21 Sitzen aus der Wahl hervor. Ihr Oppositionsbündnis vereint insgesamt 48 Mandate auf sich.
Opposition auf arabische Parteien angewiesen
Das Ergebnis führt zu einem Patt im Parlament - und zu einer schwierigen Regierungsbildung. Um eine Mehrheit von 61 Sitzen zu erreichen, wäre Eisenkots Oppositionslager rechnerisch auf die Unterstützung der vorwiegend arabischen Parteien angewiesen. Diese erzielten mit zusammen 19 Mandaten ein historisch gutes Ergebnis.
Eine Zusammenarbeit mit arabischen Vertretern könnten jedoch Teile des Oppositionsbündnisses - insbesondere die jüdischen Parteien - ablehnen. Eisenkot selbst knüpft eine Regierungsbildung an strikte Bedingungen. Mögliche Partner müssen demnach ein Bekenntnis zum jüdischen und demokratischen Charakter des Staates Israel unterzeichnen, eine allgemeine Dienstpflicht anerkennen und die islamistische Hamas als Terrororganisation einstufen.
In der kommenden Woche will Staatspräsident Jitzchak Herzog den Auftrag zur Regierungsbildung erteilen - entweder an Netanjahu oder an Eisenkot.
Eisenkot: Netanjahu will Wahlergebnisse delegitimieren
Unterdessen warf Eisenkot dem bisherigen Regierungschef Netanjahu vor, das Ergebnis der Parlamentswahl infrage stellen zu wollen. "Es ist bereits klar, dass Likud und Netanjahu eine koordinierte, organisierte Kampagne gestartet haben, die darauf abzielt, die Ergebnisse der Wahl zu delegitimieren", sagte Eisenkot am Donnerstag in einer Videobotschaft.
Netanjahus Regierung hatte angesichts historischer Zugewinne israelisch-arabischer Parteien bei der Parlamentswahl auf Ermittlungen gegen diese wegen angeblicher Finanzierung aus dem Ausland gedrängt. "Die Wahlen in Israel wurden gestohlen", erklärte die Likud-Partei. Es gehe um einen "Anschlag auf die Demokratie" mit dem Ziel, Israel zu "islamisieren und die rechte Regierung zu stürzen".
Der rechtsextreme Sicherheitsminister Itamar Ben-Gvir forderte zudem die Festnahme der Chefs der israelisch-arabischen Parteien. Zur Begründung verwies er darauf, dass sie verdächtigt würden, "Geld aus Katar" erhalten zu haben.
Untersuchungen des Geheimdienstes laufen
Die Wahlkommission hatte den Geheimdienst mit Blick auf die Vorwürfe am Mittwochabend zu Untersuchungen aufgefordert. Bislang wurden öffentlich keine Belege für die Anschuldigungen vorgelegt.
Der Inlandsgeheimdienst Shin Bet bestätigte, dass die Untersuchung laufe, betonte aber, es gehe nicht darum, "eine ganze Gemeinschaft zu beschuldigen, die auf demokratische und legale Weise gewählt hat".
Mit Informationen von Tim Aßmann, ARD-Hauptstadtstudio, zzt. Tel Aviv

title: Bundespräsident Steinmeier verbindet Grundsatzrede in Peking mit symbolischem Tischtennis-Auftritt
content_c:
Steinmeier wirbt für China-Handel auf Augenhöhe
29. Oktober 2026
Steinmeiers letzte Reise nach Asien erweist sich zunehmend als eine Art "Derisking-Mission" gegenüber dem schwierigen Partner im fernen Osten. Bei der Rede an der Universität Beida am dritten Tag seines Besuches, wo ihm auch die Ehrenprofessur verliehen wurde, geht es vor allem um Wirtschaft und Politik. Bei der Fragerunde spricht er aber auch Chancen einer gesellschaftlichen Annäherung an, die sich durch Kooperation in Kultur, Wissenschaft und Sport ergeben.
Mit Respekt und klaren Erwartungen
An der renommierten Hochschule zollt Steinmeier dem Gastgeberland Respekt für seinen Aufstieg zur Weltmacht. Zugleich formuliert er klare Erwartungen an China: "Mit Größe und Macht kommt große Verantwortung", sagt der Bundespräsident vor einem Saal voller Studenten. "Wir haben keine Sorge davor, dass China aufsteigt. Wir blicken darauf, wie China aufsteigt".
Seine These: Mittel- und längerfristig brauchen nicht nur Mittelmächte, wie Deutschland, sondern auch die großen Mächte wie China, eine regelbasierte internationale Ordnung. Steinmeier ruf dazu auf, diese Ordnung "gemeinsam zu stärken und für Frieden und freien Welthandel einzutreten".
Keine Abkopplung, aber Win Win für beide
Der Bundespräsident fordert Wirtschaftsbeziehungen auf Augenhöhe und appelliert darum, die Ungleichgewichte im Wirtschaftsverhältnis zwischen China und Europa abzubauen. "Wir wollen keine Abkopplung von China, sondern im Gegenteil: Wir wollen den Handel so gestalten, dass er für beide Seiten weiterhin Vorteile bringt." Dafür brauche man faire und einheitliche Regeln.
Damit spielt er auf die hohen Hürden europäischer Unternehmen, die auf dem chinesischen Markt aktiv sein wollen. Da China seine Exporte nach Europa stark subventioniert, gelänge der europäische Markt zu schnell unter Druck. Darin bestünde "die Gefahr einseitiger Verwundbarkeit", so Steinmeier. Europäer könnten das für ihre Wirtschaft nicht wollen, ebenso wie "China es für seine Wirtschaft nicht will".
Ukraine-Krieg: Appell an China
In seiner Rede geht es auch um Chinas Rolle als ständiges Mitglied im UN-Sicherheitsrat und gegenüber Russland. Steinmeier appelliert, China solle auf Russland einwirken und helfen, ein Ende des Ukraine-Krieges herbeizuführen. Insbesondere, da China enge Beziehungen zu Russland habe.
Nach Steinmeiers Worten stünden bei diesem Krieg, ähnlich wie auch im Nahen Osten, auch die Interessen Chinas auf dem Spiel. Als große Handelsmacht brauche es auch freie Seewege, intakte Lieferketten und eine sichere Energieversorgung. "Je länger diese Konflikte andauern, desto schwächer wird die gesamte Weltwirtschaft insgesamt und damit auch eine ihrer größten Volkswirtschaften, nämlich China."
Steinmeier geht auch auf Zukunftsthemen ein, bei den China ein besonderes Interesse haben sollte: Klima und künstliche Intelligenz. Er fordert die Gastgeber auf, man solle bei KI "gemeinsam internationale Leitplanken setzen, damit die Technologie vom Menschen beherrschbar bleibt", so der Bundespräsident.
Tischtennis als Brücke zwischen den Gesellschaften
Nach der Rede folgt der weniger offizielle Teil des Besuchs: In der Sporthalle der Universität tritt Steinmeier zu einer kurzen Partie Tischtennis gegen Timo Boll an. Der frühere Weltklassespieler genießt auch in China große Bekanntheit. Als prominenter Gast begleitet er den Bundespräsidenten auf seiner Reise.

content:
Steinmeier wirbt für China-Handel auf Augenhöhe
29. Oktober 2026
Steinmeiers letzte Reise nach Asien erweist sich zunehmend als eine Art "Derisking-Mission" gegenüber dem schwierigen Partner im fernen Osten. Bei der Rede an der Universität Beida am dritten Tag seines Besuches, wo ihm auch die Ehrenprofessur verliehen wurde, geht es vor allem um Wirtschaft und Politik. Bei der Fragerunde spricht er aber auch Chancen einer gesellschaftlichen Annäherung an, die sich durch Kooperation in Kultur, Wissenschaft und Sport ergeben.
Mit Respekt und klaren Erwartungen
An der renommierten Hochschule zollt Steinmeier dem Gastgeberland Respekt für seinen Aufstieg zur Weltmacht. Zugleich formuliert er klare Erwartungen an China: "Mit Größe und Macht kommt große Verantwortung", sagt der Bundespräsident vor einem Saal voller Studenten. "Wir haben keine Sorge davor, dass China aufsteigt. Wir blicken darauf, wie China aufsteigt".
Seine These: Mittel- und längerfristig brauchen nicht nur Mittelmächte, wie Deutschland, sondern auch die großen Mächte wie China, eine regelbasierte internationale Ordnung. Steinmeier ruf dazu auf, diese Ordnung "gemeinsam zu stärken und für Frieden und freien Welthandel einzutreten".
Keine Abkopplung, aber Win Win für beide
Der Bundespräsident fordert Wirtschaftsbeziehungen auf Augenhöhe und appelliert darum, die Ungleichgewichte im Wirtschaftsverhältnis zwischen China und Europa abzubauen. "Wir wollen keine Abkopplung von China, sondern im Gegenteil: Wir wollen den Handel so gestalten, dass er für beide Seiten weiterhin Vorteile bringt." Dafür brauche man faire und einheitliche Regeln.
Damit spielt er auf die hohen Hürden europäischer Unternehmen, die auf dem chinesischen Markt aktiv sein wollen. Da China seine Exporte nach Europa stark subventioniert, gelänge der europäische Markt zu schnell unter Druck. Darin bestünde "die Gefahr einseitiger Verwundbarkeit", so Steinmeier. Europäer könnten das für ihre Wirtschaft nicht wollen, ebenso wie "China es für seine Wirtschaft nicht will".
Ukraine-Krieg: Appell an China
In seiner Rede geht es auch um Chinas Rolle als ständiges Mitglied im UN-Sicherheitsrat und gegenüber Russland. Steinmeier appelliert, China solle auf Russland einwirken und helfen, ein Ende des Ukraine-Krieges herbeizuführen. Insbesondere, da China enge Beziehungen zu Russland habe.
Nach Steinmeiers Worten stünden bei diesem Krieg, ähnlich wie auch im Nahen Osten, auch die Interessen Chinas auf dem Spiel. Als große Handelsmacht brauche es auch freie Seewege, intakte Lieferketten und eine sichere Energieversorgung. "Je länger diese Konflikte andauern, desto schwächer wird die gesamte Weltwirtschaft insgesamt und damit auch eine ihrer größten Volkswirtschaften, nämlich China."
Steinmeier geht auch auf Zukunftsthemen ein, bei den China ein besonderes Interesse haben sollte: Klima und künstliche Intelligenz. Er fordert die Gastgeber auf, man solle bei KI "gemeinsam internationale Leitplanken setzen, damit die Technologie vom Menschen beherrschbar bleibt", so der Bundespräsident.
Tischtennis als Brücke zwischen den Gesellschaften
Nach der Rede folgt der weniger offizielle Teil des Besuchs: In der Sporthalle der Universität tritt Steinmeier zu einer kurzen Partie Tischtennis gegen Timo Boll an. title: Особисте життя Даші Астаф'євої: роман з відомим співаком, розірвані заручини і стосунки з молодшим коханим
content_c:
Особисте життя Даші Астаф'євої: роман з відомим співаком, розірвані заручини і стосунки з молодшим коханим
Пропонуємо дізнатися, що відомо про особисте життя Даші Астаф’євої, яке вона ретельно приховує.
Українська співачка, модель і волонтерка Даша Астаф’єва не з тих, хто охоче ділиться подробицями особистого життя.
Артистка дотримується думки, що «щастя полюбляє тишу». Проте все ж таки деякі подробиці знаменитості не вдалося приховувати. Зокрема, у Даші Астаф’євої був роман із відомим співаком, про який взагалі ніхто не знав. Також артистка розривала заручини. А зараз знаменитість щаслива у стосунках зі значно молодшим айтівцем.
Редакція сайту ТСН.ua пропонує дізнатися, що відомо про особисте життя Даші Астаф’євої.
Таємний роман із відомим співаком Мішею Крупіним
У Даші Астаф’євої та Міші Крупіна був непублічний роман. Вперше артисти розповіли про це влітку 2021 року. Щоправда, коли саме тривали їхні стосунки, лишається загадкою. Парочка говорить, що зустрічалась у «далекому минулому».
Однак більше відомо про причини їхнього розриву. Міша Крупін розповів, що на це вплинули деякі фактори. По-перше, складність характерів, зокрема, його. Артист говорить, що йому тяжко реагувати на зауваження. По-друге, у парочки були взаємні претензії одне до одного. Врешті, непорозуміння накопичились, тож Даша Астаф’єва вирішила поставити крапку.
Міша Крупін говорить, що розірвати стосунки — було правильним рішенням. Вони відпустили минулі образі та стали друзями.
Коханий під слідством та розірвані заручини
2016 року Даша Астаф’єва зав’язала стосунки з підприємцем Артемом Кімом. Цей роман знаменитості вже був публічним. Стосунки доволі швидко розвивались, що 2017 року пара вже заручилась. Однак весілля так і не відбулося.
У серпні 2017 року Артема Кіма затримали детективи НАБУ. Чоловіка підозрювали у розкраданні державних коштів на суму майже 27 млн грн під час тендеру на закупку техніки Південноукраїнською АЕС. Сама ж Даша Астаф’єва не вірила у причетність коханого до злочину, підтримувала його та відвідувала судові засідання.
Однак 2021 року співачка поставила крапку в цих стосунках та розірвала заручини. Артистка пояснила це тим, що їхні почуття не витримали випробувань та втручань чужих людей. Окрім того, у пари більше не було ресурсу будувати сім’ю. Попри розрив, Даша Астаф’єва та Артем Кім залишились друзями.
Стосунки із загадковим айтівцем, який молодший за Дашу Астаф’єву
Вже під час повномасштабної війни в Україні Даша Астаф’єва закрутила новий роман, про який вона вперше розповіла навесні 2022 року. Обранцем знаменитості став айтівець, який значно молодший за неї. Щоправда, Даша не розкриває імені коханого та не показує його фото. Артистка пояснила, що мала досвід публічних стосунків, тож тепер хоче тримати особисте життя подалі від камер.
Проте деякі подробиці все ж таки відомі. Парочка познайомилась доволі випадково у спортзалі, після цього все й закрутилось. Співачка зізнавалась, що саме коханий став її рятівним колом. Обранець не давав на початку війни опустити Даші руки, підтримував та стимулював рухатися вперед.
До речі, разом із обранцем знаменитість започаткувала бізнес — книжковий застосунок UnderBooks, користувачі якого можуть послухати твори українських письменників. Саме коханий надихнув Дашу Астаф’єву втілити в реальністю цю ідею.
Нагадаємо, раніше редакція сайту ТСН.ua писала історію кохання ведучою Олени-Христини Лебідь та екснардепа Павла Розенка. Пропонуємо дізнатися, як пара таємно заручилась та чому не одружується.

title: Хэллоуин: что можно делать на праздник
content_c:
В ночь с 31 октября на 1 ноября во многих странах отмечают Хэллоуин. В Украине этот праздник официально не отмечается, но многие наши граждане любят связанные с ним традиции.
Традиции празднования
Этот праздник имеет традиции, берущие свое начало со времен кельтов Ирландии и Шотландии. Они были связаны с завершением сбора урожая. Раньше считалось, что в этот день открывается граница между миром живых и мертвых, и тени умерших проникают на землю. Чтобы защититься от них, разжигали костры и надевали страшную одежду.
В древности на Хэллоуин приносили в жертву животных. Также считалось, что необходимо принести домой кусочек священного пламени и разжечь с его помощью костёр. До наших дней эти традиции не сохранились.
В современном мире на праздник принято надевать костюмы, но они уже не обязательно должны быть страшными. На Хэллоуин сейчас уже не разжигают костры. Вместо них делают Джека — из тыквы вырезают страшную рожу, в которую ставят свечу. Также можно использовать просто свечи. Особенно — красного цвета.
Также на Хэллоуин принято просить сладости. В праздник дети, одетые в костюмы, ходят от дома к дому и кричат «Конфеты или смерть!» (Trick or treat!).

title: "Продовжуйте рух". Стало відомо, чому в Іспанії потяг на шаленій швидкості врізався в інший і загинуло 68 людей
content_c:
"Продовжуйте рух". Стало відомо, чому в Іспанії потяг на шаленій швидкості врізався в інший і загинуло 68 людей
  - Author, Відділ новин
  - Role, BBC News Україна
- Published
- Час прочитання: 5 хв
Іспанські ЗМІ оприлюднили записи переговорів між машиністами та диспетчерським центром за кілька хвилин до катастрофи 28 жовтня. В цей день швидкісний поїзд, що прямував із Мадрида до Севільї, врізався в потяг, який стояв на колії. Унаслідок зіткнення загинули щонайменше 68 людей, десятки зазнали поранень.
На борту одного з поїздів, який експлуатує державна компанія Renfe, перебували 397 пасажирів. Попереду нього на тій самій лінії був поїзд приватної компанії Iryo, у якому було 147 пасажирів.
За попередніми даними, через збій у системі автоматичної сигналізації, тобто через комп'ютерну несправність, усі поїзди на цій ділянці зупинили.
Однак, за словами міністра транспорту Іспанії, згодом поїзду Renfe "помилково" дали дозвіл продовжити рух.
Аудіозаписи розмов між диспетчерським центром на вокзалі "Аточа" в Мадриді та двома машиністами оприлюднили іспанські ЗМІ, зокрема El País і RTVE.
Із них можна зробити висновок, що одному швидкісному поїзду дали дозвіл на рух попри те, що інший потяг, який перебував приблизно за 25 км попереду, зупинився.
В одному із записів диспетчер наказує машиністу поїзда Renfe AVE відновити рух на звичайній швидкості після усунення технічних несправностей.

Машиніст уточнює: "На звичайній швидкості?"
Диспетчер відповідає: "Так".

Як повідомляє El País, на високошвидкісній магістралі Мадрид–Севілья, де сталася катастрофа, нині проводять масштабну модернізацію. У рамках цього систему LZB замінюють на більш досконалу Європейську систему управління рухом поїздів (ERTMS).
Водночас безпека на залізниці не залежить від якоїсь однієї технології, а лінія, де сталася трагедія, оснащена й іншими системами, зазначає видання.
Bloqueo de Señalización Lateral (BSL) — це резервна система інтервального регулювання руху поїздів, яку використовують у разі збою автоматичної системи сигналізації або передавання даних.
На ще одному аудіозаписі машиніст іншого поїзда, компанії Iryo, повідомляє диспетчеру, що зв'язок із системою керування поїздом втрачено і потяг не рухається.
"Поїзд стоїть перед вхідним світлофором на станції Урда", — каже машиніст диспетчеру. Після обміну репліками диспетчер дає вказівку "продовжити рух" у штатному режимі.
Згідно з пізнішим записом, машиніст Iryo знову зв'язується з диспетчерським центром і повідомляє, що, як і раніше, не може зрушити поїзд з місця.
"Система [безпеки] не піддається керуванню. Тому я й далі стою перед вхідним світлофором", — пояснює він.
Цей запис свідчить про те, що диспетчера повідомили: поїзд Iryo залишається на місці в той час, коли до нього наближається склад компанії Renfe.
El País зазначає, що поїзд AVE отримав вказівку відновити рух о 8:36, ще до того, як підтвердили, що поїзд Iryo почав віддалятися.

Пізно ввечері в середу родичі й далі намагалися зібрати інформацію про пасажирів, які перебували в потягах.
Цивільна гвардія Іспанії відкрила пункти в Мадриді, Толедо, Севільї та Кордові для опрацювання повідомлень про зниклих безвісти.
"Пріоритет — встановлення особи зниклих безвісти та взяття зразків ДНК, щоб знайти їхніх родичів", — йдеться в повідомленні служби в соцмережі X.
У Брюсселі приспустили прапори Європейського Союзу. Європейська комісія назвала це "знаком європейської солідарності" в період жалоби в Іспанії.

title: Перша леді США Меланія Трамп заявила про завершення розмінування маршрутів для гуманітарного конвою до Олешок
content_c:
Заходи з розмінування узгоджених дорожніх маршрутів для проходження гуманітарного конвою до тимчасово окупованого міста Олешки Херсонської області повністю завершені, а підготовка до доставки допомоги мешканцям перебуває на фінальному етапі, повідомила перша леді США Меланія Трамп у четвер увечері.
"Операції з розмінування завершені, а підготовка до гуманітарної місії перебуває на завершальному етапі. Усі визначені маршрути, створені спільно Україною та Росією, очищені для безпечного проїзду. Конвой незабаром увійде до Олешок, щоб доставити їжу, чисту воду, ліки та іншу необхідну допомогу жителям міста", – написала вона у соцмережі X.
Як повідомлялося, з 3:00 вівторка, 27 жовтня, Україна запровадила режим припинення вогню у визначеному районі тимчасово окупованих Олешків виключно для проведення гуманітарної операції з доставки допомоги мешканцям та підготовки до вільного виїзду цивільного населення.
В свою чергу, у четвер німецьке видання Bild із посиланням на українських військовослужбовців поінформувало, що гуманітарне перемир'я триває за посередництва Ватикану та першої леді США, проте російські окупаційні війська використовують режим тиші для прихованого перегрупування сил і підготовки наступу на Херсон після завершення перемир'я 1 листопада.

content:
Заходи з розмінування узгоджених дорожніх маршрутів для проходження гуманітарного конвою до тимчасово окупованого міста Олешки Херсонської області повністю завершені, а підготовка до доставки допомоги мешканцям перебуває на фінальному етапі, повідомила перша леді США Меланія Трамп у четвер увечері.
"Операції з розмінування завершені, а підготовка до гуманітарної місії перебуває на завершальному етапі. Усі визначені маршрути, створені спільно Україною та Росією, очищені для безпечного проїзду. Конвой незабаром увійде до Олешок, щоб доставити їжу, чисту воду, ліки та іншу необхідну допомогу жителям міста", – написала вона у соцмережі X.
Як повідомлялося, з 3:00 вівторка, 27 жовтня, Україна запровадила режим припинення вогню у визначеному районі тимчасово окупованих Олешків виключно для проведення гуманітарної операції з доставки допомоги мешканцям та підготовки до вільного виїзду цивільного населення.
В свою чергу, у четвер німецьке видання Bild із посиланням на українських військовослужбовців поінформувало, що гуманітарне перемир'я триває за посередництва Ватикану та першої леді США, проте російські окупаційні війська використовують режим тиші для прихованого перегрупування сил і підготовки наступу на Херсон після завершення перемир'я 1 листопада.

title: Audio reveals exchanges between Spain train operators and drivers moments before deadly crash
content_c:
Audio reveals exchanges between Spain train operators and drivers moments before deadly crash
- Published
Leaked audio recordings that were published in Spanish media have revealed conversations between train drivers and a control centre just minutes before a deadly crash on Wednesday morning, that has killed 69 people.
Officials are investigating the cause of the disaster, which occurred when a train from Madrid to Seville barrelled into a stationary train near Urda.
Three audio recordings between Madrid's control centre and two train drivers appear to show that one high-speed train was given clearance to move even though another train had stalled on the track, about 25km (15 miles) ahead.
Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez has said that authorities will "get to the bottom of every last detail of this tragedy".
Dozens of people were injured, with survivors recounting harrowing scenes people crying and bleeding, passengers trapped in their seats, missing limbs and smoke billowing throughout the carriages, one of which caught fire.
On Thursday, Spain's King Felipe VI and Queen Letizia visited some of the injured passengers in a hospital in Toledo.
He later expressed condolences to the victims' relatives, pledging that the investigation would determine why the crash happened, and what measures would be taken for this not to happen again.
- Young athlete and former minister among victims of Spain train crash 
  - Published8 hours ago
The crash is one of the worst rail disasters in Europe's modern history, and Spain's worst crash since 2013. On Thursday, the country began three days of national mourning.
The moving train, run by state-owned operator Renfe, had 397 passengers on board. The stationary train was run by private operator Iryo, and carrying 147 passengers.
A reported issue with the automatic signalling system - a computer failure - had forced all trains to halt on the affected stretch.
But later the Renfe train was ordered to proceed in "error", according to Spain's transport minister.
The audio recordings were published by several Spanish news outlets including El Pais and RTVE.
In one, a control centre operator is speaking to the driver of the Renfe train, which was having some technical difficulties.
After some exchanges, the control operator tells the driver: "Continue your journey and then proceed under [Lateral Signalling Block], at normal speed with normal operation."
The driver replies: "At normal speed?" To which the controller answers: "Yes."
The Lateral Signalling Block is a back-up or alternative train system used when the automatic signalling or data transmission system fails.
The driver of the stationary Iryo train says in another audio recording that communication with the train-control system has been lost, and it is not moving.
The train "is stationary in front of the entry signal at Urda", the driver tells the control centre operator. After a series of exchanges, the driver is then told to "resume the journey" normally.
The Iryo driver then contacts the control centre again, according to a later recording, saying they cannot start the train. "The train won't allow me to control the [security] system. That's why I am still stopped in front of the entry signal," they say.
The latter recording suggests that the controller had been notified that the Iryo train remained stationary as the Renfe train approached.
Iryo said its carriages were "struck from behind" by the other train.
Spain's transport minister Óscar Puente said on Wednesday that the decision to instruct the trains to move again, without any speed restrictions, was "inexplicable".
The leaking of the audio recordings has been criticised by some Spanish politicians, with Alberto Ibáñez, a member of Congress for the left-wing Sumar platform, writing on X that they were "despicable".
Irene Montero - the prime ministerial candidate for the left-wing Podemos party - said responsibility for the crash should not be placed on one worker, adding that train drivers and experts have been warning against the liberalisation of the railway sector for years.
From the crash site, Sánchez said: "We are working day and night not only to support the victims' families, but also to establish every last detail of this tragedy and strengthen safety measures to ensure it never happens again."
Most Spanish politicians have cancelled all public engagements and suspended their campaigning ahead of a snap election on 29 November.
The exception is the far-right party Vox. Its leader, Santiago Abascal, said his party would not take part in what he described as attempts to "use mourning to silence criticism" of the country's rail infrastructure.
Overnight, around 1,500 people gathered outside the Spanish transport ministry building in the capital, according to broadcaster TVE, which reported that demonstrators were largely calling for the resignations of Sánchez and Puente.
Police used tear gas to disperse crowds after protesters hurled bottles and flares. No injuries or arrests were reported.
Rail drivers went ahead with a planned strike on Thursday, with the Spanish Union of Railway Drivers (Semaf) saying the strike action was being held "in defence of railway safety".
The leader of Spain's main opposition People's Party Alberto Núñez Feijóo said: "Spain has the right to know what is happening with its infrastructure."
At the crash site, emergency crews worked through the night under powerful floodlights to cut open metal carriages in the search for victims, with many of those killed in the crash still to be identified.
Hundreds of personnel have been deployed to the disaster site to assist with recovery efforts, Spain's interior ministry said, with drones and helicopters being used to find victims and remove rubble.
A spokesperson for the Spanish Civil Guard told the BBC they had deployed more than 900 people from different specialist departments, and the priority now was identifying the deceased.
They said they did not know how long this would take, but urged those with missing family members to go to one of the local centres which have been set up to offer DNA samples.

title: Further delays for major council overhaul in nine of 14 proposed areas
content_c:
Further delays for major council overhaul in nine of 14 proposed areas
- Published
The government has announced further delays to nine of 14 major council mergers, with only five now going ahead.
Proposals for 14 regions to undergo mergers of smaller councils to form larger unitary authorities was put on hold by Local Government Secretary Angela Rayner last month, following concerns around legal challenges.
Local Government Minister Jim McMahon has told MPs the review had found the government's decision-making to be "robust", but nine areas have now been withdrawn for further review.
Only five of the original 14 regions will be taken forward, after three more weeks of consultation. Shadow local government secretary Katie Lam condemned the latest news as "a farce".
Mergers will continue to progress in East Sussex, Gloucestershire, Oxfordshire, Warwickshire and Worcestershire.
But the government is seeking "legal clarity" in the remaining nine areas, which are: Derbyshire, Devon, Hertfordshire, Kent, Lancashire, Leicestershire, Lincolnshire, Nottinghamshire, and Staffordshire.
In a Commons statement, McMahon said the government was "withdrawing the decisions announced in July" for those nine areas.
"I want to be absolutely clear that this is not a reflection of the work underpinning those proposals," he added.
The review will now focus on the nine areas where current plans have been withdrawn for further review, as well as four areas where plans were withdrawn in September, in Essex, Hampshire, Norfolk and Suffolk.
Two further areas, Cambridgeshire and West Sussex, are still waiting for merger plans to be agreed, totalling 15 regions where local government reorganisation plans remain undecided.
McMahon said: "We will move faster where we can, and some of the remaining areas may receive an outcome decision before others.
"I commit to coming back to the House with updates for another set of areas by Christmas, and every area will have an outcome by early next year."
Reconfirming local elections in May 2027 would go ahead on existing council boundaries, he announced plans for elections to shadow councils, set to run for a year before taking over from old authorities, will now be held in May 2028.
Responding, Lam set out how the reorganisation had been beset by delays over the past two-and-a-half years.
"From start to finish this government's approach to local government reorganisation has been nothing short of a farce," she told MPs.
She added: "Naturally the taxpayer was left to pick up the tab for all of these delays - a bill which runs into the tens of millions of pounds."
Local Government Association chair Eamonn O'Brien called for a re-set of relations between the government and local councils across the country.
He said: "While today's announcement provides some certainty for some areas, many councils remain frustrated by the situation they have been placed in.
"All councils affected need urgent clarity on next steps and how costs already incurred will be met.
"There needs to be a reset in the relationship between government and councils on local government reorganisation, with local government fully engaged in shaping decisions from the outset."
- All change for Oxfordshire and West Berkshire councils 
  - Published13 hours ago
- Plans for major overhaul of councils halted 
  - Published7 September
- Rayner promises mayor for every region of England 
  - Published16 December 2024
- New councils to be created in 14 areas of England 
  - Published16 July

title: I earn £30,000. I'm angry there was no fuel duty cut in the Budget
content_c:
I earn £30,000. I'm angry there was no fuel duty cut in the Budget
- Published
Chancellor John Healey has unveiled his first Budget.
He announced £100 energy payment for millions and a tax rise on banks, among other measures.
BBC News has been speaking to people on a range of incomes on how they feel about their finances and how the Budget affects them.
Dave Herbert is a professional driver on £30,000 a year. He moves cars between showrooms and does deliveries and says fuel prices have been "crazy" this year.
He spends around £350 a month on petrol for work and personal use. That's 40% to 50% more than at the start of the year, he says.
He has to commute into Cardiff, a 62-mile round trip from his home in Ynysddu. "I'd love to have a hybrid car but even an entry-level used car is too expensive."
The 48-year-old, who is married with a 12-year-old daughter, says he has to find the extra money for fuel "from an already tight budget" and "dreads" filling up at the pump.
The only measure Dave wanted to see was a cut to fuel duty, and he was disappointed this didn't happen.
"I'm pretty angry, really. Nothing has been thrown my way," he says.
The main fuel duty rate has been frozen at 52.95p per litre until the summer, but Dave says: "It sounds like they're giving us something by keeping it frozen but they're actually still taking it off us."
'I get £4,062 a year. I'm frustrated there's no action on NEETs yet'
Emily Nelson completed her A-levels last year and like thousands of her peers has been unable to find a job since leaving college.
The 19-year-old from Swindon wants to be an animator but in the meantime is applying for retail and sales roles and apprenticeships. Most of the time, she doesn't hear back from potential employers.
"I'm trying my best, it's all you really can do. It's kind of suffocating in a way. You see everyone else managing, and you feel like you're not."
Emily was initially disappointed with the Budget, and then frustrated that the government is waiting for the outcome of a review into youth unemployment before legislating next year.
"I'm glad the government is aware, and that they have a plan," she said. "But it's a bit frustrating that we have to wait a little longer to find out what it is."
However, she adds: "It's not happened today, but it will happen."
She wants to see more funding to businesses so they can take on more young employees. She'd also like to see more money for training and the government's Jobs Guarantee, external scheme extended.
The scheme, being rolled out across England, Scotland and Wales, guarantees fully funded, six-month paid jobs for 18 to 24-year-olds who have been on universal credit and looking for work for 18 months. But Emily thinks people should be eligible after a year.
'I earn £22,000. Cost-of-living help doesn't go far enough'
Robert Portlock, 29, has always lived with his parents in Gateshead and would love to move out. But he doesn't think he can afford to.
Rent would be his biggest concern, he says, explaining that a small flat in his area would cost him about two-thirds of his monthly wage.
"Council tax and energy bills would add to it. Food too. I'd need a TV licence, broadband, my car and some money to socialise. By that point I'd be in the minus."
Robert's biggest expense currently is his car, which he says he needs for his 32-mile round trip to work at Newcastle Airport. But he's paying £750 a month in car finance, insurance, fuel and tax.
The Budget "doesn't go far enough", he says, adding he would have liked to have seen more help with the cost of living, including a cut in fuel duty.
The £100 household energy allowance over a year is less than £10 a month, he says, while action on tariffs on food items will save only £21 a year, or £1.75 per month.
"What am I going to buy with that - a Freddo?"
He would like to get on the housing ladder but for now it feels a distant prospect. The government has announced a scheme to help first-time buyers in England who have a deposit of 2.5%. It also confirmed plans for a new First Time Buyer Isa, external, to replace the Lifetime ISA, which will see the government contribute towards the cost of a first home.
But Robert says neither policy will make much difference to him. "You can't save if you don't have money. They seem to be acting as if inflation hasn't happened."
'I earn £41,000. Energy support will definitely help'
Chloe Chin-Saad's husband passed away four years ago and her biggest worry is the cost of living.
She's very grateful that the rent she pays on her south London maisonette is set below the market rate as it is housing association accommodation, but says life was easier when she shared the bills. "Two incomes make a massive difference."
She lives with her 16-year-old son, and says her energy bill has risen sharply over the past year and she now pays about £200 a month on gas and electricity.
"We try to be more aware, we think more about how long we run the hot water when we do the dishes."
Chloe, 40, and her son have cut back on luxuries like going to M&S and the cinema, and she now tries to limit the weekly food shop to £40.
But she can't do anything to reduce her £200 council tax bill, the £250 a month she pays on car finance, or the amount she spends on medicines for her various health conditions, including rheumatoid arthritis.
Two mobile phone bills, and food and pet insurance for her dog also add to her costs. She says the amount she has left over at the end of each month varies, and sometimes she is left with as little as £50.
Chloe says she is "pretty happy" with the Budget, and that "small changes give me hope".
Cutting standing charges on gas, and the £100 household energy payment for households in council tax bands A to D this winter are "definitely going to help", she says.
"It was quite a thoughtful Budget," she adds. "I can see, in years to come, light at the end of the tunnel."
'I earn £150,000. Higher earners like me should've been taxed more'
Jonathan Whitwam, who recently joined the Labour Party, works in finance and says, in addition to his mortgage, his biggest outgoing is supporting his two daughters through university. He and his wife, who live in Essex, pay their rent, which is around £18,000 per year.
His daughters will start their working lives with between £45,000 to £60,000 of debt each, plus interest, which will be compounding at £5,000 to £8,000 per year.
"I have no objection to paying for degrees as I think they are a great way of broadening horizons and having great life experience. But I think the interest should be waived or capped below 1%, otherwise it's a noose around their neck for a substantial part of their lifetime."
Jonathan, 52, says the Budget was "very safe", reducing energy costs for his household by getting rid of standing charges, while cutting bills for many people this winter.
However, he wanted taxes to be put up for higher earners like himself in the name of "redistribution" and says there was "nothing" in the Budget on that.
"If we want better roads, hospitals, schools we need to raise more tax," he adds.
'I have a £15,000 pension. I'm even Stevens after the Budget'
Christine Morris, from Worksop, has been retired for eight years and lives on a state pension combined with a small private pension her late husband left her.
"It is very difficult to balance the books," the 78-year-old says. "I do go on holiday, but I'm spending more of my savings to live."
The chancellor said standing charges would be removed from gas bills, but Christine, who has a gas boiler, says it's not clear yet whether she will benefit, because those costs will be added on to the unit rate.
However, she says the £100 household energy payment will help over the winter
"I'm not sure I'll be better off," she says. Instead she thinks she will be "even Stevens".
She was unconvinced by Andy Burnham's pledge to end the triple lock so that from 2030 the state pension will rise at least by inflation or 2.5%, with the money saved used to create a free-at-the-point of use national care service for England sometime "in the next parliament".
Christine thinks the new service will take time to come in. In the meantime, she fears she will "get less pension and still have to pay out the same for any care I need".

The scheme, being rolled out across England, Scotland and Wales, guarantees fully funded, six-month paid jobs for 18 to 24-year-olds who have been on universal credit and looking for work for 18 months. But Emily thinks people should be eligible after a year.
'I earn £22,000. Cost-of-living help doesn't go far enough'
Robert Portlock, 29, has always lived with his parents in Gateshead and would love to move out. But he doesn't think he can afford to.
Rent would be his biggest concern, he says, explaining that a small flat in his area would cost him about two-thirds of his monthly wage.
"Council tax and energy bills would add to it. Food too. I'd need a TV licence, broadband, my car and some money to socialise. By that point I'd be in the minus."
Robert's biggest expense currently is his car, which he says he needs for his 32-mile round trip to work at Newcastle Airport. But he's paying £750 a month in car finance, insurance, fuel and tax.
The Budget "doesn't go far enough", he says, adding he would have liked to have seen more help with the cost of living, including a cut in fuel duty.
The £100 household energy allowance over a year is less than £10 a month, he says, while action on tariffs on food items will save only £21 a year, or £1.75 per month.
"What am I going to buy with that - a Freddo?"
He would like to get on the housing ladder but for now it feels a distant prospect. The government has announced a scheme to help first-time buyers in England who have a deposit of 2.5%. It also confirmed plans for a new First Time Buyer Isa, external, to replace the Lifetime ISA, which will see the government contribute towards the cost of a first home.
But Robert says neither policy will make much difference to him. "You can't save if you don't have money. They seem to be acting as if inflation hasn't happened."
'I earn £41,000. Energy support will definitely help'
Chloe Chin-Saad's husband passed away four years ago and her biggest worry is the cost of living.
She's very grateful that the rent she pays on her south London maisonette is set below the market rate as it is housing association accommodation, but says life was easier when she shared the bills. "Two incomes make a massive difference."
She lives with her 16-year-old son, and says her energy bill has risen sharply over the past year and she now pays about £200 a month on gas and electricity.
"We try to be more aware, we think more about how long we run the hot water when we do the dishes."
Chloe, 40, and her son have cut back on luxuries like going to M&S and the cinema, and she now tries to limit the weekly food shop to £40.
But she can't do anything to reduce her £200 council tax bill, the £250 a month she pays on car finance, or the amount she spends on medicines for her various health conditions, including rheumatoid arthritis.
Two mobile phone bills, and food and pet insurance for her dog also add to her costs. She says the amount she has left over at the end of each month varies, and sometimes she is left with as little as £50.
Chloe says she is "pretty happy" with the Budget, and that "small changes give me hope".
Cutting standing charges on gas, and the £100 household energy payment for households in council tax bands A to D this winter are "definitely going to help", she says.
"It was quite a thoughtful Budget," she adds. "I can see, in years to come, light at the end of the tunnel."
'I earn £150,000. Higher earners like me should've been taxed more'
Jonathan Whitwam, who recently joined the Labour Party, works in finance and says, in addition to his mortgage, his biggest outgoing is supporting his two daughters through university. He and his wife, who live in Essex, pay their rent, which is around £18,000 per year.
His daughters will start their working lives with between £45,000 to £60,000 of debt each, plus interest, which will be compounding at £5,000 to £8,000 per year.
"I have no objection to paying for degrees as I think they are a great way of broadening horizons and having great life experience. But I think the interest should be waived or capped below 1%, otherwise it's a noose around their neck for a substantial part of their lifetime."
Jonathan, 52, says the Budget was "very safe", reducing energy costs for his household by getting rid of standing charges, while cutting bills for many people this winter.
However, he wanted taxes to be put up for higher earners like himself in the name of "redistribution" and says there was "nothing" in the Budget on that.
"If we want better roads, hospitals, schools we need to raise more tax," he adds.
'I have a £15,000 pension. I'm even Stevens after the Budget'
Christine Morris, from Worksop, has been retired for eight years and lives on a state pension combined with a small private pension her late husband left her.
"It is very difficult to balance the books," the 78-year-old says. "I do go on holiday, but I'm spending more of my savings to live."
The chancellor said standing charges would be removed from gas bills, but Christine, who has a gas boiler, says it's not clear yet whether she will benefit, because those costs will be added on to the unit rate.
However, she says the £100 household energy payment will help over the winter
"I'm not sure I'll be better off," she says. Instead she thinks she will be "even Stevens".
She was unconvinced by Andy Burnham's pledge to end the triple lock so that from 2030 the state pension will rise at least by inflation or 2.5%, with the money saved used to create a free-at-the-point of use national care service for England sometime "in the next parliament".
Christine thinks the new service will take time to come in. In the meantime, she fears she will "get less pension and still have to pay out the same for any care I need".
Get in touch
What are you hoping for from the Budget? What questions do you have?

title: China expels a record number from Communist party amid Xi’s intensified purges of top officials
content_c:
China expelled a record number of officials from the Chinese Communist party (CCP) as it concluded a major political gathering, which saw an unprecedented number of empty seats indicating the scale of the purges under Xi Jinping.
A record 33 members were expelled at this week’s fifth plenum, a gathering of top officials that takes place roughly once a year.
Just 279 of the full and alternate members of the CCP’s Central Committee attended this week’s gathering, compared with the 376 originally named as members in 2022. That means that more than 25% of the original cohort were absent, many due to purges. It is the highest number of “empty chairs” at the plenum in modern Chinese history.
The confirmed expulsions included Zhang Youxia, the former second-in-command to China’s leader in the military hierarchy, and Ma Xingrui, the former party secretary for Xinjiang. Other absences were unexplained.
“More empty seats underscores the plenum’s focus on Xi’s vision of strict internal discipline,” said Neil Thomas, a senior fellow at the Asia Society thinktank, in a post on X.
The theme for this week’s plenum was party governance. Since coming to power in 2012 Xi has focused on stamping out corruption in the party. But in recent years the campaign has intensified, taking out officials in the highest ranks of the party and the military, raising questions about if the campaign is also a tool to remove political rivals or punish disloyalty.
Xi appears to have grown increasingly frustrated with what he sees as a lack of discipline in the ranks of the party that wields absolute authority over the state and society in China. Earlier this year he said that the party must uproot “sick trees” and that the fight against corruption was a “never-ending journey”.
A series of purges has gutted the seven-man Central Military Commission, the ruling body of China’s People’s Liberation Army. There are now just two members left: Xi himself, and the military’s anti-graft tsar, Zhang Shengmin.
Zhang was promoted to the politburo of the CCP this week, the highest ruling body in the party. Zhang is now the only military member of the senior leadership body.
The plenum also laid the groundwork for the 21st Party congress, an event which happens every five years and is expected to next be held in the second half of 2027. Xi is expected to secure a fourth term as leader of the party, making him the longest ruler of Communist China since Mao Zedong.
The ranks of the Central Committee and the politburo will be refreshed at next year’s congress, but many analysts believe that recent purges have been so wide-ranging that there are few suitable candidates to be promoted.

title: Reform UK launches its own ‘newspaper’ with Farage on front page
content_c:
Reform UK has launched what it is calling a newspaper, featuring large pictures of Nigel Farage, which the party hopes will replace mainstream media for its supporters.
Though the party is hiring qualified journalists to write its newspapers, the only “reporter” credited with writing articles is Farage, the party leader.
Political parties often put out pamphlets made to look like newspapers in local areas during elections, but it is unusual for a party to put out a paper nationally, year-round. The party has said it wishes to build a “significant national publishing operation” as well as its TV channel hosted on YouTube.
In his first column for the publication, Farage writes: “We have had enough of what we say and do being distorted by the media. So instead, we want to talk to you directly, and make sure that you get our message straight from the Reformer.”
Its front-page story features a photograph of Farage smiling and posing with a labrador, with the headline “Nigel Farage: we will fix broken Britain”.
Other stories include “Clacton result: Farage 22,239, Establishment 0.” This refers to the byelection called by Farage after he resigned his Essex seat following revelations about an undeclared £5m gift from the crypto billionaire Christopher Harborne. The gift was revealed by the Guardian earlier this summer. The other main parties declined to stand in the ensuing byelection, with the result that Farage’s main opponent was Count Binface.
One piece advertises Reform’s plan to use the Royal Navy to send back migrants who travel across the Channel in small boats. It says: “A Reform UK government will launch Operation Fortress. Prime Minister Nigel Farage will order the Royal Navy to stop the boats and return the illegal immigrants to France. Not one will make it to Britain.” Military experts have criticised this plan, saying the navy should not be used as a ferry service.
Other articles include a short tribute to Ann Widdecombe, the Reform politician who was killed in her home in July, featuring a quote from Farage, and another piece by Farage in which he vows to declare a national emergency should he become prime minister. Other features include updates on local Reform politicians’ progress on filling in potholes and picking up litter.
Reform insiders said the first edition was “rushed” and to expect more news and features in subsequent editions, coming monthly.
Roles at the publication are still open, with 12 journalist jobs including executive editor, website editor and multimedia reporters/producers advertised online.
Reform sources said they thought the newspapers, being delivered to homes across Britain and available in the lobby of the party’s Westminster office, would drive up membership rates. Those who join the party using the cut-out form included in the newspaper are offered a free mug and badge.
Rather than being kept on the news stands in the lobby of Millbank Tower, where Reform has its headquarters, the Reformer is kept behind the desk at reception and available on request. The party says the paper has been sent to 15 million people across the country.
Readers of the publication are also urged to sign up as Reform candidates in the May 2027 local elections.
A report by Printweek revealed that the paper has been printed by Walstead Group, which has contracts with several of the UK’s leading newspapers including the Sunday Times and Sun on Sunday.
The paper is reportedly being led by Mick Hume, the founder and former editor of the online libertarian-right politics magazine Spiked, and is part of Reform’s drive to build a “national publishing operation” with a digital newsroom and expanded video content.
Though the first edition of the free paper does not appear to contain any exclusive news stories, budding reporters hoping to join the Reformer need to be able to produce scoops.
A job advert states: “Reform UK is building a seven-day digital newsroom at its Westminster headquarters and is looking for hard-working, NCTJ-qualified multimedia reporter/producers who can report, write and publish high-quality content at speed. The role sits at the heart of the party’s ambition to build the Reform UK website into a significant national publishing operation.”
It adds that applicants need to come up with original stories “rather than relying solely on rewriting or republishing material already available elsewhere”.
